datatype.name: AtomicNumber
datatype.definition: The proton number Z of a chemical element: a positive integer that uniquely identifies the element (1 for hydrogen, increasing by one across the periodic table).

datatype.name: StandardAtomicWeight
datatype.definition: The standard atomic weight (relative atomic mass) of an element: a dimensionless ratio conventionally expressed in unified atomic mass units (u, the dalton; 1 u = 1/12 of the mass of a carbon-12 atom). Modelled as a local decimal rather than a wmoop.core Mass quantity because it is a relative, dimensionless mass, not an absolute one, so no SI dimension or unit from the core kernel applies.

enumeration.name: StateOfMatter
enumeration.definition: The macroscopic physical state in which a substance presents under given conditions.

provenance.source: Original WMOOP definition
provenance.note: The three classical macroscopic states; plasma and further states are depth-on-demand.

value.definition: Fixed shape and fixed volume; constituent particles held in a rigid arrangement.
Fixed volume but no fixed shape; particles mobile while remaining in contact.
Neither fixed shape nor fixed volume; particles widely separated and free-moving.

concept.name: ChemicalSubstance
concept.definition: A form of matter with a definite chemical composition and characteristic properties.

provenance.source: IUPAC. Compendium of Chemical Terminology (the 'Gold Book')

property.name: standardState
property.definition: The physical state of the pure substance at standard ambient temperature and pressure (298.15 K, 100 kPa).

provenance.source: Original WMOOP definition
provenance.note: Per-substance values are sourced at L2.

property.name: meltingPoint
property.definition: The temperature at which the pure substance passes from the solid to the liquid state at standard pressure.

provenance.source: Original WMOOP definition
provenance.note: Per-substance figures are sourced at L2.

concept.name: ChemicalElement
concept.definition: A substance whose atoms all share the same number of protons and that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.

provenance.source: IUPAC. Compendium of Chemical Terminology (the 'Gold Book')

property.name: atomicNumber
property.definition: The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom of the element (its proton number, Z); the element's defining property.

provenance.source: IUPAC. Compendium of Chemical Terminology (the 'Gold Book')

property.name: symbol
property.definition: The one- or two-letter IUPAC-approved symbol identifying the element (e.g. H, Fe).

provenance.source: IUPAC. Nomenclature of Inorganic Chemistry (the 'Red Book', IUPAC Recommendations 2005)

property.name: standardAtomicWeight
property.definition: The standard atomic weight of the element, averaged over the isotopic composition of normal terrestrial material.

provenance.source: IUPAC Commission on Isotopic Abundances and Atomic Weights (CIAAW), Standard Atomic Weights 2021

concept.name: ChemicalCompound
concept.definition: A substance made of two or more different chemical elements chemically bonded in a fixed proportion.

provenance.source: IUPAC. Compendium of Chemical Terminology (the 'Gold Book')

property.name: chemicalFormula
property.definition: A formula expressing the compound's constituent elements and their proportions (e.g. H2O).

provenance.source: IUPAC. Nomenclature of Inorganic Chemistry (the 'Red Book', IUPAC Recommendations 2005)

concept.name: Atom
concept.definition: The smallest particle of a chemical element that retains that element's chemical identity.

provenance.source: IUPAC. Compendium of Chemical Terminology (the 'Gold Book')

concept.name: Molecule
concept.definition: An electrically neutral group of two or more atoms held together by chemical bonds, the smallest unit of a molecular substance.

provenance.source: IUPAC. Compendium of Chemical Terminology (the 'Gold Book')

concept.name: ChemicalReaction
concept.definition: A process in which one or more chemical substances (reactants) are transformed into one or more different substances (products).

provenance.source: IUPAC. Compendium of Chemical Terminology (the 'Gold Book')

property.name: isReversible
property.definition: Whether the reaction can proceed in both the forward and reverse directions under the same conditions.

provenance.source: Original WMOOP definition
provenance.note: Flags the Gold Book notion of a reversible reaction; per-reaction values are sourced at L2.

role.name: Catalyst
role.definition: The role of a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without itself being consumed by it.

provenance.source: IUPAC. Compendium of Chemical Terminology (the 'Gold Book')

individual.name: Hydrogen
individual.definition: The chemical element with atomic number 1, the lightest element.

provenance.source: IUPAC Periodic Table of the Elements (2021)
IUPAC CIAAW, Standard Atomic Weights 2021

individual.name: Carbon
individual.definition: The chemical element with atomic number 6, the structural basis of organic chemistry.

provenance.source: IUPAC Periodic Table of the Elements (2021)
IUPAC CIAAW, Standard Atomic Weights 2021

individual.name: Oxygen
individual.definition: The chemical element with atomic number 8.

provenance.source: IUPAC Periodic Table of the Elements (2021)
IUPAC CIAAW, Standard Atomic Weights 2021

individual.name: Iron
individual.definition: The chemical element with atomic number 26, a transition metal (Latin ferrum).

provenance.source: IUPAC Periodic Table of the Elements (2021)
IUPAC CIAAW, Standard Atomic Weights 2021
